sections.content: How many people stayed in Crook after gaining qualifications?

Crook is a small town in the North East. Crook does not have its own university.

Crook has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Crook ended up with:

  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 435 state-school pupils from Crook who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 105 (24%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 125 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Crook to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Crook's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Crook in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Crook's GCSE cohort:

  • 25 graduates left the North East

In 2018 to 2019, 38% of qualified non-graduates living in Crook had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 120 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Crook, compared with the 125 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 63% of qualified (level 3+) non-graduates in Crook had also lived there when they sat their GCSEs, while 38% had moved there from elsewhere.
